Noah Rivera: Quick Q 1 1 moving to Tallinn for 10 weeks for partner's assignment, planning to keep working remotely for Redwood. Do I need to change my home base now or can I wait until we land? How will the monthly WFH stipend, health coverage, and payroll taxes behave?
Tori (People Ops): Congrats! Short answer: you can declare homebase now or on arrival. Payroll/benefits treat the effective date you enter on the Homebase Change form as the cutover. If you stay on US payroll, stipend proration and benefits remain for that period; taxes may still be owed in Estonia depending on days present.
Noah Rivera: Im aiming to stay on US payroll for the 10-week stay. Any red flags?
Ramon (Payroll): If you stay on US payroll, 401(k) deferrals/match continue but we have to model withholding and potential double taxation. We need move dates and visa info. Cutover lead time for a local payroll is ~4-6 weeks if Redwood activates an entity/EO. For a temporary stay, retaining US payroll is common.
Mei (Benefits): If you remain on US medical, carriers often limit routine care abroad. HSA contributions usually require US tax filing and may be suspended while living overseas. Ill open a benefits case and confirm specifics with the carrier.
Noah Rivera: Also have a lot of baby gear to ship. Is there any ad-hoc relocation assistance?
Tori (People Ops): We dont provide standard movers for personal moves. We can pre-approve reasonable one-off reimbursements case-by-case. DM me rough estimates and Ill confirm.
PeopleOps Bot: Reminder: Homebase Change form draft saved (autosave).
Ramon (Payroll): Next step: Noah submit Homebase Change form with requested effective date and "retain US payroll" option. Ill run a 10-week projection for stipend/proration and tax-withholding scenarios.
Noah Rivera: Submitted the form and DMd the shipping estimate. Thanks all!
